channel.title: Supercharged Daily
channel.description: Original Tesla, SpaceX and xAI reporting, plus tracker changes.

item.title: SpaceXSI credits Grok Voice with 5 million patient calls at Innovaccer. Innovaccer's own release says those came first
item.description: Healthcare software company Innovaccer is adding Grok Voice to its patient-calling AI agents. SpaceXSI's post pairs the deal with "over 5M patient interactions," but Innovaccer's release describes that figure as its own voice AI's growth before Grok. What the deal covers and what's only a roadmap.

item.title: "52% dilution" in a SpaceX-Tesla deal doesn't mean 52% more shares. I ran the math from both companies' filings
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX shares fell again on Wednesday as investors weighed a possible all-stock merger. Gary Black's widely quoted "52% dilution" figure checks out, but several outlets described it as SpaceX issuing 52% more shares. Using the share counts in both 10-Qs, the issuance would be more than double that.

item.title: SpaceX turns down its BEAD money and offers to serve those homes for $0. What the government's new contract actually requires
item.description: NTIA published a model "zero outlay" agreement on 23 Nov for a low-orbit provider that serves its BEAD locations without taking the subsidy, and NTIA's head says SpaceX has agreed to it. I read the 15-page contract: free equipment, 100/20 Mbps, ten years, and a lot less paperwork.

item.title: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites as orbital data centers, the first such authorization in U.S. history
item.description: The FCC on 25 Nov 2026 granted SpaceX authorization to deploy up to 1 million Starmind orbital compute modules, the first U.S. authorization for a constellation of data centers in space, according to an official Commission release posted by Chairman Brendan Carr. The grant authorizes deployment. It does not set a launch timetable.

item.title: A space jellyfish is a rocket plume lit by sunlight while the ground is still dark. The best window is 30 to 60 minutes before sunrise or after sunset
item.description: A space jellyfish forms when a rocket's high-altitude exhaust is still in sunlight and the observer is already in darkness. Vandenberg officials, who also call it twilight phenomenon, say it usually appears two to three minutes after a launch 30 to 60 minutes before sunrise or after sunset. USSF-380 this Saturday is a night launch, not a twilight one.

item.title: The EU has postponed its Tesla Assisted Driving meeting to December 15. A rejection would invalidate national approvals already granted
item.description: A European Commission spokesperson told Reuters on 25 Nov 2026 that the EU meeting expected to consider bloc-wide approval of Tesla Assisted Driving has been postponed until December 15. A rejection at EU level would invalidate the national approvals already granted. No reason was given.

item.title: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok's sexualized images. Here's what the two complaints actually claim
item.description: Two state attorneys general filed consumer-protection suits against SpaceX, SpaceXSI and X over Grok-generated sexual images, including of children. I read both complaints: the claims, the penalties allowed, and what X says in response.

item.title: Tesla's official Robotaxi page now shows more than 6 million autonomous miles. The last dated safety results still stop at 3.1 million on 18 Oct
item.description: On 24 Nov, Tesla's live Robotaxi counter stood at more than 6.01 million autonomous miles. The official safety results still cover 22 Jan to 18 Oct, when the fleet had driven 3.1 million miles.

item.title: FSD v15 is in owners' cars. The release notes, who has it, and what "25x" actually measures
item.description: Tesla started rolling out FSD (Supervised) v15.0.1 on Saturday, hours after Musk said wide release was next month. So far it's reaching HW4 Model Ys in the US. I went through the release notes and Tesla's three different ways of describing its 25x claim.

item.title: Musk: AI5 goes to Optimus and cars stay on AI4. AI4.5 loses 8GB of planned RAM because memory got expensive
item.description: Over one Sunday of replies on X, Elon Musk said Tesla's AI5 chip is going to Optimus, cars will remain on AI4, AI4 now costs twice as much because of memory prices, and the planned AI4.5 board was cut from 32GB to 24GB of RAM. Here's how that fits what Tesla said on its last two earnings calls.

item.title: Tesla wants a Texas tax break for a $3.1 billion polysilicon plant near Corpus Christi. Here's what its application says
item.description: Tesla has applied under Texas's JETI program for a school-tax limit on a proposed $3.1 billion polysilicon refinery near Robstown in Nueces County. The filing promises 515 jobs by 2032 and says Tesla may build elsewhere without the incentive. I went through the numbers.

item.title: SpaceX turned pad 4E around in 32 hours. USSF-266 made three national security missions from the pad in about 83 hours 48 minutes
item.description: NROL-136 lifted off from Vandenberg's SLC-4E on Sunday, 32 hours after USSF-317, which SpaceX says is its fastest turnaround between launches from the same pad. USSF-266 launched from the same pad at 11:08am ET on Tuesday, and the booster landed on Of Course I Still Love You on its 29th flight.

item.title: Musk says built-in Starlink could reach every Tesla by late 2027. New Cybercabs already have it in the trunk lid
item.description: Elon Musk said on Sunday that embedded Starlink across Tesla's lineup is "hopefully" coming toward the end of next year, except in China. Tesla's own Cybercab first-responder guide, dated 20 Nov, says Cybercabs built from November 2026 already carry it.

item.title: Arizona's attorney general wants Cochise County to hold off on SpaceX's 6 GW campus vote
item.description: In a 19 Nov letter, Attorney General Kris Mayes asked the Cochise County Planning and Zoning Commission to delay its 9 Dec vote on SpaceX's special use permit SU26-22 until state and federal regulators have reviewed it. A town hall is set for 3 Dec.

item.title: SpaceX has applied to excavate 5.2 million cubic yards at Pecan Island. Louisiana has opened public comment through 16 Dec
item.description: The state's official public notice for coastal use permit P20260831 describes a Gulf wharf, barge docks, dredging and an access road at the end of Highway 3147. The application is under review, not approved. How to comment by 16 Dec.

item.title: Italy approves Tesla Assisted Driving, the 12th EU country and the first big one. The EU math still doesn't add up
item.description: Italy's transport ministry gave Tesla's supervised Assisted Driving a provisional approval ahead of the EU process. It's the 12th EU country and the first of the big four, taking the group from 15.5% to 28.6% of the EU population.

item.title: Mexico has collected 5.9 kg of debris after Flight 15. SpaceX says most of the viral posts are fabrications
item.description: Mexico's Profepa says 5.9 kg of debris has been collected after Flight 15, while SpaceX says most viral posts are fabrications.

item.title: South Korea won't review Tesla's FSD request for Shanghai-built cars yet. Tesla sent five pages by email
item.description: South Korea's transport ministry says Tesla's FSD exemption application for Shanghai-built cars isn't ready for review, after Tesla emailed five pages.

item.title: Anthropic closes its IPO at $93.5 billion and takes SpaceX's record outright. Its new cash nearly matches its SpaceX compute deal
item.description: Anthropic's IPO closed at about $93.5 billion after underwriters bought all 147 million optional shares, passing SpaceX's record, and a $26 billion placement takes its new cash close to its SpaceX compute deal.

item.title: Cybercab rides start in Dallas, the second city after Austin, and Tesla kept its "next month" promise
item.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account says the Cybercab has arrived in Dallas, keeping a mid-October 'next month' promise. Tesla has not given a Dallas fleet size, service area, hours or rider rules.

item.title: Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO beats SpaceX's base deal, and its prospectus still owes SpaceX $3.1 billion a month
item.description: Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 and opened at $111.50 as of 11:53 a.m. ET on 19 Nov. That beats SpaceX's $75 billion base deal; the all-time record still depends on Anthropic's option.

item.title: Grok Bot now books flights, hotels and rental cars. What it checks before you pay, and where it hands back to you
item.description: SpaceXSI's Grok Bot can now book flights, hotels and rental cars. The changelog adds a bags, changes and refunds panel, and sends you the airline link if a purchase can't be confirmed.

item.title: Cameron County says no to SpaceX's 10-year tax break for its $24 billion Starbase compute plant. SpaceX warns of a "revenue cliff"
item.description: Cameron County commissioners voted 3–2 not to hold a hearing on a 10-year, 100% tax abatement for SpaceX's $24 billion Starbase compute plant. SpaceX warned of a revenue cliff. The 39% comparison is the author's estimate.

item.title: 200 Cybercabs in one batch put Tesla ahead of Waymo on Texas's robotaxi register, 1,507 to 1,321, as of 18 Nov
item.description: Texas DMV records now list 1,507 Tesla Robotaxi vehicles, 773 of them Cybercabs, against Waymo's 1,321. A single batch of 200 Cybercabs with 2027 model-year VINs did it. Registered isn't the same as carrying riders.

item.title: Tesla's Powercore puts a transformer, breaker and inverter in one box. First units run in 2027
item.description: Tesla Energy's Powercore is a solid-state medium-voltage unit rated 7.4 MW that replaces a battery site's or data center's separate transformer and inverter. Tesla says first units operate in 2027; there's no price, factory or customer yet.

item.title: SpaceXSI gave five accounting jobs to Grok Bots. What each one does, and what still needs a person
item.description: SpaceXSI says five Grok Bots now run its order-to-cash process, cutting invoice time from about 24 hours to minutes. Refunds and credits still need a person to sign off, and the time savings are SpaceXSI's own estimates.

item.title: Nvidia's first results without Huang say Vera Rubin is "coming online soon" at SpaceXSI
item.description: Nvidia posted $115.8 billion of Q3 revenue and guided $130 billion for Q4. Its release says Vera Rubin NVL72 racks run at five clouds and are "coming online soon at SpaceXSI." SpaceX's own $40 billion Vera Rubin lease doesn't start until 2027.

item.title: Delta's CEO says most Starlink airlines "haven't even started yet." United has it on 635 jets
item.description: Ed Bastian says customers don't pick airlines for Wi-Fi and that most airlines promising Starlink haven't started. The numbers say otherwise, and Delta's Amazon Leo plan just lost 40 satellites on a failed Vulcan launch.

item.title: Ramaphosa tells Musk to follow South Africa's rules. Musk calls them racist. Here's where Starlink's licence stands
item.description: South Africa's president said in California that Starlink must follow local ownership rules. Musk replied that the country is "super racist." The real fight is over a 30% rule, a stalled policy fix and a court case filed on 9 Nov.

item.title: Tesla's €3 billion Berlin hall is sized for 1 million Cybercabs a year. EU rules allow 1,500
item.description: Tesla plans a new Cybercab building at Giga Berlin: about €3 billion, construction from early 2027, production in 2029, room for up to 1 million a year. It's a plan, and the EU still caps driverless cars at 1,500 per type a year.

item.title: SpaceX is now Nvidia's biggest stock holding, and Nvidia was still buying
item.description: Nvidia's 13F for the quarter to 30 Sep shows 130.5 million SpaceX shares worth $19.7 billion, 40.7% of its stock portfolio and now ahead of Intel. Nvidia added 7.7 million SpaceX shares while cutting Intel by a quarter.

item.title: Tesla nearly doubles its Miami Robotaxi zone, but Waymo still covers 2.5 times as much ground
item.description: Tesla's Robotaxi zone in Miami now reaches downtown and Brickell. Trackers put it at about 59 square miles, up roughly 90%. Waymo's Miami area has been 150 square miles since May.

item.title: Starship V4 by the numbers: a 70-meter ship, nine engines and propellant at a quarter of the price per ton
item.description: A day after SpaceX caught a ship for the first time, Elon Musk gave the first firm size for the next version: about 70 meters long, more than 60% more propellant and nine engines instead of six. These are plans, not hardware. Here's how they compare with the V3 ship SpaceX lists today.

item.title: Fifteen flights to a caught ship: every Starship flight, explosions included
item.description: Starship's first flight in April 2023 ended with SpaceX commanding its flight termination system on a tumbling rocket. On Saturday, Nov 14, 2026, the tower at Starbase caught a Starship upper stage for the first time. This is the whole run, flight by flight, including the vehicles SpaceX lost on the way.

item.title: The Pentagon is paying SpaceX $9.9M to study a laser-link mismatch in its missile-tracking satellites
item.description: The Space Development Agency awarded SpaceX $9,921,992 to study how its Plaser laser terminal can carry data from missile-tracking satellites that use a different optical standard. What was bought, what wasn't, and why a small contract points at a big problem.

item.title: The Grok Bot team says it shipped 11,000 pull requests in a month. Here's how, and what the numbers leave out
item.description: In a talk posted 14 Nov, Grok Bot engineer Lauren Tan said her team merged 11,000 pull requests in a month with about 0.5% reverted, and that agents now merge most of their own code. The method, the math, and the caveats.

item.title: Grok Imagine moves into the main Grok chat, a day after reports that most of its team was cut
item.description: On 14 Nov, @imagine said image and video creation is "now live in Grok" and @grok said more SpaceXSI products are being pulled into "one Grok experience." What changed, what the official pages now say, and what nobody has said yet about the old Imagine screens, the layoffs report and the Odyssey movie.

item.title: Musk says his Nvidia deals ran on Jensen Huang's word. Here's how much of SpaceX's AI now rests on Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 11 Nov. Elon Musk says many of Huang's supply deals were handshakes and some "will be lost," while Nvidia's board says customer commitments continue "without interruption." A look at SpaceX's Nvidia exposure: about 860,000 GB300s in Memphis by Musk's count, a $40 billion Vera Rubin lease, Google's $920 million a month GPU rental and the Starmind satellites.

item.title: Starship Flight 15 recap: the first ship catch, and a booster lost in the Gulf
item.description: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase on Friday, Nov 13, at 5:48 p.m. ET (2:48 p.m. PT), deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and spent about 22 hours in orbit. On Saturday at about 4:21 p.m. ET (1:21 p.m. PT), Mechazilla caught the ship at the tower, the first time a Starship upper stage has been returned to the launch site and caught. Super Heavy Booster 22 diverted to a Gulf splashdown; photos later showed the hull tipped over and broken in the water.

item.title: SpaceX reportedly cut most of the Grok Imagine team, a week after Starlink asked fans to make an ad with it
item.description: The Information reports about 60 people on Grok Imagine were laid off in the past week, leaving a handful to run it. The tool made 2 billion videos a month in Q1, Starlink is running an Imagine ad contest, and Musk's Odyssey movie deadline is 47 days away. No company statement yet.

item.title: A Helsinki taxi firm bought 100 Model Ys to run on Tesla Assisted Driving, and says it will publish every time a driver steps in
item.description: Menevä, a Finnish taxi company with more than 1,000 cars, is starting Robo Menevä in Helsinki: 100 Tesla Model Ys on Tesla Assisted Driving, a licensed "host" up front who stays legally responsible, and a public map of every takeover. Rides haven't started yet (as of 14 Nov 2026).

item.title: Starship Flight 15: the booster diverted, the ship is in orbit, and the first ship catch is due today
item.description: Starship Flight 15 launched Nov 13 at 5:48 p.m. ET and put 26 Starlink V3 satellites in orbit, but Super Heavy Booster 22 diverted to a Gulf splashdown instead of a catch. The ship is set to try the first-ever ship catch at Starbase around 4:21 p.m. ET (1:21 p.m. PT) on Nov 14 (as of 14 Nov 2026, 3:44 a.m. ET).

item.title: Invited customers can now order a Cybercab for $29,990. The $299 a month is the real price
item.description: Tesla has started inviting select customers to buy a Cybercab for personal use: $29,990, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, a required $299/month autonomy subscription and December 2026 delivery in five Texas cities (as of 14 Nov 2026). Musk already says the fee is too high.

item.title: SpaceX's $50 billion Arizona compute campus: 6 GW, no turbines, and a zoning vote on Dec 9
item.description: SpaceX has published its plan for a 6 GW supercomputing campus in Cochise County, Arizona: nine buildings, a 24 GWh battery, dry cooling and a $50 billion pledge (as of 13 Nov 2026). How it differs from the gas-fired Starbase plan, and what the county decides on Dec 9.

item.title: Grok Bot on Mac can now use Messages, Mail and Notes. Here's how it compares with the phone app
item.description: Grok Bot's Mac app can now connect to seven Apple apps, including Mail and Notes, which the phone version doesn't list. What each permission allows, what's missing, and which one to think twice about.

item.title: Bloomberg says SpaceX and Tesla talks have moved to terms, with a December announcement possible (as of 12 Nov 2026)
item.description: Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources, said on 12 Nov 2026 that SpaceX and Tesla boards are negotiating terms and governance, with an announcement as soon as December or early 2027. Neither company has confirmed this. At Thursday's closes, a no-premium swap works out to about 2.84 SPCX shares per TSLA share. That figure is a calculation, not a reported term.

item.title: Nonprofits sue SpaceXSI and four other AI labs to freeze frontier AI. What a freeze could mean for Grok 4.8
item.description: Four nonprofits filed suit in San Francisco on 12 Nov 2026 asking a judge to bar Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI from building anything more capable than what they had that day. What the complaint alleges about Grok. This is a complaint; no judge has ruled.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi now runs 24/7 in all eight cities (as of 11 Nov 2026)
item.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account says rides now run around the clock in every city where the service operates, as of 11 Nov 2026. That's 168 hours a week, up from 112 at the end of August. The 2am close lasted 12 days. When I wrote that change up, I projected 24/7 around New Year's Eve if Tesla kept its August-to-October pace. It got there about 50 days sooner.

item.title: Grok Bot 1.0 is out: shared Bots, Slack and Teams, and Bots in your meetings
item.description: SpaceXSI took Grok Bot out of beta on 11 Nov 2026. Version 1.0 lets a whole team share one Bot, use it inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, and bring it into video calls. The company also says Bots will now spot work and offer to do it. How well the new team features work is still the company's claim.

item.title: Musk moves the Cybertruck’s end date again, to the end of summer 2027 (as of 11 Nov 2026)
item.description: Elon Musk says Cybertruck production will now run through the end of summer 2027 to work through more of the backlog. That’s the third timeline in six days, and roughly two more months than the eight months he gave on 9 Nov 2026.

item.title: Starlink Mini 2 vs Mini: thinner, heavier, and finally a battery
item.description: Starlink’s Mini 2 adds a 71 Wh quick-swap battery, USB-C power and Wi-Fi 6, as reported from its spec sheet. It is 40% thinner and about a pound heavier than the original Mini with kickstand. Invite-only US preorders are a $999 bundle with a year of Roam Unlimited, as reported.

item.title: Finland approves Tesla Assisted Driving, making it 11 EU countries (as of 11 Nov 2026)
item.description: Finland’s Traficom has recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla Assisted Driving, formerly FSD (Supervised). That makes 11 EU countries, about 15.5% of the EU population as of 1 Jan 2026. Tesla says rollout begins soon, with no date.

item.title: Security firm says 94.7% of live Grok Build apps opened without sign-in, including 24 from SpaceXSI staff (as of 10 Nov 2026)
item.description: Claroc, which sells security for AI-built apps, says 35,578 of 37,571 live Grok Build apps opened for anyone as of 10 Nov 2026, including 24 built by SpaceXSI and X staff, which were pulled after reporters asked. This is a report, not a proven breach.

item.title: FCC accepts SpaceX’s 800 MHz applications for filing. Comments are due 1 Dec 2026
item.description: The FCC has accepted SpaceX’s applications to take control of Grain Management’s 546 paired 800 MHz licenses for filing. That starts the review; it is not approval. Comments are due 1 Dec 2026, and the build-out rules Grain agreed to would pass to SpaceX if the transfer is approved.

item.title: SpaceX orders solar-cell factory gear from Germany, and Musk says 100 GW a year is already ordered (as of 10 Nov 2026)
item.description: SINGULUS says it has signed a contract with SpaceX for a turnkey heterojunction solar-cell line as SpaceX expands satellite manufacturing in Bastrop, Texas, with the first line worth more than €60 million and due in the first half of 2027. SpaceX and SINGULUS say production will scale to support more than 100 GW of equipment. Musk says 100 GW a year is already ordered.

item.title: Tesla comments on NHTSA’s plan to overhaul U.S. headlight rules, asking that cameras, software and more automaker seats be covered (as of 10 Nov 2026)
item.description: Tesla’s 9 Nov 2026 comment on NHTSA’s notice of intent to form a committee to modernize FMVSS 108 asks that the overhaul cover camera-guided matrix LED headlights and over-the-air changes, and that more automaker seats be added. This is a public comment, not a petition for rulemaking. No rule has changed.

item.title: Grok 4.8 is in RL on a homemade C stack, with a soft Bot rollout pledged later this week (as of 10 Nov 2026)
item.description: Elon Musk says SpaceXSI dropped JAX and SGLang for its own C/C++ code, Grok 4.8 pre-training is done and the model is now in RL (as of 10 Nov 2026). He pledged a soft rollout to Grok Bot users later this week, with no date, benchmarks or pricing yet.

item.title: SpaceX wants a tax break for a $24 billion gas plant and super-compute facility at Starbase (as of 6 Nov 2026)
item.description: A City of Starbase notice says SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility on about 444 acres by the Port of Brownsville, with about $24 billion for the first phases (as of 6 Nov 2026). Two of the city's three commissioners work for SpaceX. Nothing is approved yet; a hearing is set for 9 Dec 2026.

item.title: Tesla pulls the Premium AWD Cybertruck. The Cyberbeast is the only trim left, at $109,990 (as of 10 Nov 2026)
item.description: Tesla stopped Premium AWD Cybertruck orders on Monday night and raised the Cyberbeast US starting price to $109,990, before destination and order fees. The cheapest orderable Cybertruck has gone up $40,000 since early August (as of 10 Nov 2026).

item.title: Terafab is rush-ordering chip tools in Japan, with a plan 40 times Rapidus’s wafer capacity
item.description: Nikkei reports Terafab’s procurement team visited Japanese equipment makers, placed orders due within months, and shared a 2032 target of 1 million wafers a month — about 40 times Rapidus’s planned ~25,000 wafers a month. Reported plan, not a company announcement.

item.title: SpaceX is designing its own 5G base stations for Starlink Mobile, with Qualcomm chips inside
item.description: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon says SpaceX will build the base stations for one of the largest US 5G deployments, with Qualcomm supplying the radio silicon. Musk confirmed the partnership on X. Rollout planned from 2027; no tower deals announced.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi’s Austin zone jumps to about 442 square miles (as of 9 Nov 2026)
item.description: Tesla’s official @robotaxi account posted “Bigger Austin service area now live” with an old/new geofence map at 11:00 UTC on 9 Nov 2026. Tesla gave no square-mileage. Robotaxi Tracker measures about 442 sq mi, up from 272; RoboTracker lists 435.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi reaches San Antonio with its biggest launch zone yet, and Texas registrations are now 3 cars apart
item.description: Tesla's @robotaxi account says San Antonio rides start at 5am CT. Merritt measures the launch zone at about 275 sq mi. A 9 Nov Texas DMV pull puts Tesla at 1,282 registered driverless vehicles against Waymo's 1,285.

item.title: Grok API text gets an invisible watermark starting today
item.description: Official docs set 7 Nov 2026 as the default invisible watermark start date for seven Grok API models. Team admins can opt out; consumer app scope is not established by the API docs.

item.title: Musk says Starlink V4 lasers could outcompete undersea cables
item.description: Musk sketched Starlink V4 with about 10 times V3 capability and 10 Tb/s laser links. His interview said ten lasers; his posts discussed roughly 100 as an engineering ambition, not a settled design.

item.title: Musk says Tesla will likely rent Optimus rather than sell it
item.description: At the Baron Investment Conference on 6 Nov 2026, Elon Musk said Tesla will probably rent Optimus humanoid robots. Talk of about $30,000 falling toward $20,000 is build cost, not a rental price. Outside deliveries still point to around end of 2027.

item.title: Tesla says it arrives in Argentina on 20 November; exhibition first, sales later
item.description: Tesla confirmed an Argentina arrival date of 20 November 2026 via @Tesla_LatAm, with @Tesla and Elon Musk quoting the post. Argentine press reports an Unicenter exhibition first, with sales and test drives planned for 2027. Official posts name no models or prices.

item.title: Elon says Tesla has no government contracts, and SpaceX government work will be under 10% of revenue this quarter
item.description: Elon Musk said Tesla has no government contracts and that government revenue will be under 10% of SpaceX revenue this quarter and under 5% a year from now, quoting a Warren Redlich draft letter. Those figures are his claims on X, not filings.

item.title: Ron Baron says Elon is aiming to launch solar-powered data centers into orbit in 2027 and 2028
item.description: Investor Ron Baron told CNBC Squawk Box that Elon Musk is targeting 2027 and 2028 launches of solar-powered data centers into orbit. Elon replied: "Ron Baron understands." Investor commentary, not a SpaceX announcement.

item.title: The Tesla Model Y is Australia's best-selling passenger car through October, with 39,035 sold against 35,927 RAV4s
item.description: CarsGuide reports the Tesla Model Y sold 39,035 units in Australia from January to October 2026, ahead of the Toyota RAV4's 35,927. Elon called it the best-selling car of any kind on Earth; the figures cover Australian passenger cars only.

item.title: Tesla's chip slide renames HW4 to SI4 and sketches SI6 at 80x the compute, with Dojo 3 aimed at space
item.description: Tom's Hardware published a photographed Tesla slide renaming HW4 to SI4, listing SI5 at 40x and SI6 at 80x, with Dojo 3 aimed at space. Tesla and Musk have not posted the slide (as of 6 Nov 2026).

item.title: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab
item.description: Musk said Cybertruck production at Giga Texas winds down around mid-2027 for more Cybercab. Tesla still calls Austin the truck's home; Wes Morrill says parts and service continue (as of 6 Nov 2026).

item.title: EVgo opens its first Tesla Supercharger site. Who owns it, who runs it, and what drivers get
item.description: EVgo opened 12 Supercharger stalls in Chicago. EVgo owns and brands them; Tesla operates and maintains them under Supercharger for Business (as of 5 Nov 2026).

item.title: Tesla and SpaceX slide after the midterms. What a Democratic Congress can and can't do to the merger
item.description: SpaceX closed -3.8% and Tesla -3.3% on 4 Nov after Democrats won Congress. No merger terms yet; the new Congress seats on 3 Jan 2027 (as of 5 Nov 2026).

item.title: Dutch regulator approves Tesla's cut to the FSD speed margin, from +50% to +10%, and a new name
item.description: RDW approved Tesla's requested changes to FSD Supervised: a new name, Tesla Assisted Driving, and a driver-set speed margin capped at +10% (down from +50%). No OTA date yet; EU-wide approval still pending (as of 5 Nov 2026).

item.title: Texas elects a Democratic governor, and SpaceX's data center plans face a new risk
item.description: AP called Texas for Gina Hinojosa, who backs a data center moratorium. SpaceX aims for 3 GW by year-end and 13 GW next year, some of it in Texas (as of 4 Nov 2026).

item.title: Starlink on airlines: what the numbers actually show
item.description: JAL says Starlink and pricing helped lift ZIPAIR's passenger revenue 12.3%. What United, Alaska, Qatar, Virgin and airBaltic report about in-flight Starlink (as of 3 Nov 2026).

item.title: A SpaceX–Tesla merger could hand Musk Tesla control without hitting a single Mars or robotaxi goal
item.description: No deal exists yet, but a Reuters analysis and Tesla's filings show a SpaceX takeover could give Musk Tesla voting control while skipping his pay plan's robotaxi and robot goals.

item.title: Tesla Robotaxi launches in Fort Worth with an estimated 143-square-mile zone, but it still hasn't passed Waymo in Texas
item.description: Tesla Robotaxi opened in Fort Worth from 6am CT on 2 Nov in a zone estimated at 143 sq mi. Texas DMV lists 1,244 Teslas, 15 short of Waymo's 1,259 (as of 2 Nov 2026).

item.title: SpaceX is in talks to buy Boost Mobile, the Washington Post reports
item.description: SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, the Washington Post reports. Boost had 7.38M wireless subscribers but leases its network from AT&T and T-Mobile.

item.title: Tracker: Texas Cybercab count
item.description: Texas Cybercab registrations moved from 773 to 822. A registered car isn’t necessarily in service yet.

item.title: Tracker: Starlink McDowell snapshot
item.description: McDowell snapshot: inOrbit 11,208 → 11,203; working 11,194 → 11,189. This is a published table snapshot, not a live operator feed.

item.title: Tracker: 2026.38.6.11
item.description: 2026.38.6.11 first appeared in the Teslascope sample with 2 cars. Spotting a build isn’t the same as a wide rollout, or your car getting it.

item.title: Tracker: 2026.44.1
item.description: 2026.44.1 moved from 284 to 347 cars tracked by Teslascope. That’s Teslascope’s count, not Tesla confirming a regional rollout or that your car will get it.

item.title: Tracker: 2026.38.5.13
item.description: 2026.38.5.13 moved from 422 to 523 cars tracked by Teslascope. That’s Teslascope’s count, not Tesla confirming a regional rollout or that your car will get it.

item.title: Tracker: Flight 15 change
